method: The plan's 'NOT verified by any test' list (research/ULTRACODE-WEEK.md:46: pcr.py:33-56, 86-96, 109-123, 151-164; core.py:18-19, 33-34, 58-71; pql.py:55-73) was split into one row per rule and diffed against the docstrings and bodies of tests/test_semantics.py (31 tests, ast-extracted docstrings) and tests/test_first_class.py (9 tests). A rule counts as covered only when a named test asserts the behaviour (an exercised-but-unasserted branch is noted in the evidence). Untested rules are listed as 'missing' here and in runs/day1/untested.md; none was dropped.

findings.rule: Tick.calc rejects a duplicate id within the same tick
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:383 PCRDeclarationRulesTest.test_tick_calc_rejects_duplicate_id_within_tick (docstring 'pcr.py:43-44'; killed by `if False:` at pcr.py:43, mutation-kill.md)

findings.rule: Tick.calc coerces a str `into` to Part when called directly: pcr.tick(name).calc(..., into='px.x')
findings.evidence: no test passes a str into through Tick.calc: tests/test_semantics.py:401 uses the default into=None and :417 passes the Part OUT; PCR.calc pre-coerces at pcr.py:118 and hands the Part to Tick.calc at pcr.py:128, so every PCR-level str-into test (:328, :337, :356-357, :510-512, :529-530) stops at pcr.py:118 and never reaches pcr.py:45

findings.rule: Tick.calc wraps any binding source in Binding without a type check (silent; discriminated only at run, pcr.py:147-151)
Tick.calc appends the Invocation in declaration order, so execution order inside a tick is declaration order
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:443 PCRRunRulesTest.test_result_ref_to_unavailable_id_fails_only_at_run (a producer declared later in the same tick is 'unavailable'); tests/test_first_class.py:194-202 (cards tick lists single-card before battle-card)

findings.rule: Tick.calc stores a copy of args (dict(args or {})): args=None becomes {} and the caller's mapping is not aliased by the Invocation
findings.evidence: testimony args is asserted only for a supplied mapping (tests/test_semantics.py:441 `testimony.args == {'value': 'from-args'}`); no test asserts `args == {}` on an invocation declared without args, and no test mutates the caller's args mapping after declaration to show the Invocation (and pcr.py:171 testimony) is unaffected

findings.rule: into may be None: run publishes nothing for that invocation (pcr.py:163)
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:393-406 test_tick_calc_bypasses_pcr_duplicate_id_rule (Tick.calc without into; run completes and results['w1'] is read), :443-457 and :459-472 declare every invocation without into and run; a mutant dropping the None guard at pcr.py:163 would raise AttributeError on invocation.into.address. The None value in testimony (pcr.py:172, outside the listed ranges) is not asserted by any test

findings.rule: calc returns ResultRef(id) so the return value can be bound by a later invocation
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:377 (`ref == ResultRef('q')`), :452 (`ref == ResultRef('uses-later')`); PCR.calc returns Tick.calc's value unchanged (pcr.py:125-133)

findings.rule: ticks and the name map start empty per PCR; tick(name) creates on first mention and returns the same Tick afterwards, so later calcs join the existing tick
findings.evidence: tests/test_first_class.py:196-202 test_card_testimonies_consume_render_disc_as_fn_ref (two PCR.calc calls naming 'Cards' land in one tick holding both cards; exactly two ticks unpacked at :196); tests/test_semantics.py:459

findings.rule: _writers is per PCR: a second PCR over the same PxC binds a Part written by the first as px:, not fn:
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:538 PCRRunRulesTest.test_cross_pcr_consumer_records_px_not_fn (critic gap 12; killed by the devised globals()-shared writers mutant, mutation-kill.md row 29)

findings.rule: _ids is per PCR: two PCRs may declare the same invocation id without error
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:538-557 is the only two-PCR test and uses distinct ids ('w' and 'r'); no test declares one id in two PCRs (and no test shows that a PCR.calc rejected by Tick.calc at pcr.py:43 leaves _ids untouched, pcr.py:132)

findings.rule: tick order is first-mention order: a tick named first by a consumer runs before a tick named later by its producer
PCR.calc rejects an id already used in any tick of the same PCR
declaration-time rewrite of a Part binding into ResultRef(writer) when the writer was declared earlier in this PCR; no rewrite when the writer is declared later
PCR.calc coerces a str into to Part
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:356-363 (into='px.mid' string; the PxC value and testimony are read back), :510-519 (into='px.first' string then pxc.get('px.first')), :529-536

findings.rule: a second writer for the same into address raises ValueError; the first writer is recorded in _writers and drives the rewrite
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:320 test_pcr_multiple_writers_rejected; tests/test_first_class.py:166 test_duplicate_writer_rejected; writer registration observed through the rewrite at tests/test_semantics.py:330-344

findings.rule: a ResultRef to an id not yet in results raises ValueError at run; declaration accepts it
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:443 (same tick, producer later), :459 (producer in a later tick)

findings.rule: an fn: binding passes results[id] itself, not a copy
findings.evidence: tests/test_first_class.py:237 SharedResultFanoutTest.test_shared_mutable_result_is_not_copied_between_consumers (dict payload; deepcopy mutant killed, mutation-kill.md row 39)

findings.rule: testimony records 'fn:<id>' for a ResultRef binding
args silently override same-named bound inputs (call_args.update)
the value comes from pxc.call over the Calculation registered at pcr.py:142; two Calculation objects sharing an address with different callables make run raise
results is a flat dict keyed by invocation id; a later invocation with the same id (via Tick.calc) overwrites
into publication is immediate and per invocation: a later writer wins, earlier writes survive a mid-run failure (no rollback), and the published object is the results value
Part('') raises ValueError; any non-empty prefix is accepted
Calculation address must start with 'fn.'; the callable is not inspected
PxC.get of an unproduced address raises KeyError
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:167 PxCRulesTest.test_pxc_get_missing_raises_keyerror; reached from a PCR run at :474 test_missing_part_fails_only_at_run

findings.rule: PxC.get returns the stored object itself
set returns PxWrite kind 'new-address' then 'replacement' and overwrites in place (no versioning)
register is idempotent for the same callable and raises ValueError for a different callable at the same address, leaving the first in place
where() composes the description as '<parent> where …'
matches() materialises the selection as a tuple: empty for a missing Part, sorted by address for a prefix
values() returns every match's value in match order
one() raises ValueError unless exactly one match; returns that match's value
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantics.py:249-250 (zero -> ValueError), :264-265 (two -> ValueError); tests/test_first_class.py:143 (one match -> value)

findings.rule: optional() raises ValueError for more than one match and returns None for zero
optional() returns the single match's value when exactly one Part matches (`matches[0].value if matches`)
findings.evidence: optional() is called only with zero matches (tests/test_semantics.py:248) and two matches (:267); no test asserts the one-match return value, so a mutant `return None` at pql.py:73 would survive (one() at :143 of test_first_class.py covers the sibling path only)
